cards.front: What does one turn of the TCA cycle produce from one acetyl-CoA?
cards.back: **3 NADH**, **1 FADH2**, **1 GTP** and **2 CO2**. After oxidative phosphorylation this gives about **10 ATP**. One glucose makes **2 acetyl-CoA**, so the cycle turns twice per glucose.
cards.back_pt: **3 NADH**, **1 FADH2**, **1 GTP** e **2 CO2**. Após a fosforilação oxidativa, isso rende cerca de **10 ATP**. Uma glicose gera **2 acetil-CoA**, então o ciclo gira duas vezes por glicose.

cards.front: Which cofactors does alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase need?
cards.back: The same five as pyruvate dehydrogenase: **thiamine pyrophosphate (B1)**, **lipoic acid**, **CoA (B5)**, **FAD (B2)** and **NAD+ (B3)**. So **thiamine deficiency** and **arsenite** (which binds lipoic acid) block both enzymes.
cards.back_pt: Os mesmos cinco da piruvato desidrogenase: **pirofosfato de tiamina (B1)**, **ácido lipoico**, **CoA (B5)**, **FAD (B2)** e **NAD+ (B3)**. Por isso, a **deficiência de tiamina** e o **arsenito** (que se liga ao ácido lipoico) bloqueiam as duas enzimas.

cards.front: Where do the classic inhibitors of oxidative phosphorylation act?
cards.back: **Complex I**: rotenone. **Complex III**: antimycin A. **Complex IV**: cyanide, carbon monoxide, azide. **ATP synthase**: oligomycin. All of them **lower both O2 consumption and ATP synthesis**.
cards.back_pt: **Complexo I**: rotenona. **Complexo III**: antimicina A. **Complexo IV**: cianeto, monóxido de carbono, azida. **ATP sintase**: oligomicina. Todos **reduzem tanto o consumo de O2 quanto a síntese de ATP**.

cards.front: What do uncouplers do to oxygen consumption, ATP synthesis and body temperature?
cards.back: They let **protons** leak back across the inner membrane without passing ATP synthase. **O2 consumption rises**, **ATP synthesis falls**, and the energy is lost as **heat**. Examples: **2,4-dinitrophenol**, **aspirin overdose**, **thermogenin (UCP1)** in brown fat.
cards.back_pt: Eles deixam os **prótons** voltarem pela membrana interna sem passar pela ATP sintase. O **consumo de O2 aumenta**, a **síntese de ATP cai** e a energia se perde como **calor**. Exemplos: **2,4-dinitrofenol**, **intoxicação por ácido acetilsalicílico**, **termogenina (UCP1)** no tecido adiposo marrom.

cards.front: How does the NADH shuttle change the ATP yield of one glucose?
cards.back: **Malate-aspartate shuttle** (liver, heart, kidney): cytosolic NADH enters as NADH, about **32 ATP** per glucose. **Glycerol-3-phosphate shuttle** (skeletal muscle, brain): electrons enter as **FADH2**, about **30 ATP**. Anaerobic glycolysis gives only **2 ATP**.
cards.back_pt: **Lançadeira malato-aspartato** (fígado, coração, rim): o NADH citosólico entra como NADH, cerca de **32 ATP** por glicose. **Lançadeira do glicerol-3-fosfato** (músculo esquelético, cérebro): os elétrons entram como **FADH2**, cerca de **30 ATP**. A glicólise anaeróbia rende só **2 ATP**.

cards.front: Which enzymes remove reactive oxygen species, and what does each do?
cards.back: **Superoxide dismutase**: superoxide to H2O2. **Catalase** and **glutathione peroxidase** (contains **selenium**): H2O2 to water. **Glutathione reductase** regenerates reduced glutathione with **NADPH** from the pentose phosphate pathway (**G6PD**).
cards.back_pt: **Superóxido dismutase**: superóxido em H2O2. **Catalase** e **glutationa peroxidase** (contém **selênio**): H2O2 em água. A **glutationa redutase** regenera a glutationa reduzida com **NADPH** da via das pentoses-fosfato (**G6PD**).

cards.front: Why do mitochondrial DNA mutations mainly damage the brain, muscle and optic nerve?
cards.back: These tissues depend most on **oxidative phosphorylation**. Disease appears only when the share of mutant mtDNA in a tissue passes a **threshold** (**threshold effect**), and high-energy tissues reach that limit first.
cards.back_pt: Esses tecidos dependem mais da **fosforilação oxidativa**. A doença só aparece quando a fração de mtDNA mutante em um tecido ultrapassa um **limiar** (**efeito limiar**), e os tecidos de alta demanda energética atingem esse limite primeiro.

cards.front: What are the key features of the classic mitochondrial disorders?
cards.back: **LHON** (Leber hereditary optic neuropathy): painless, subacute central vision loss in both eyes, mostly young men. **MELAS**: myopathy, encephalopathy, **lactic acidosis**, stroke-like episodes. **MERRF**: myoclonic epilepsy, **ragged red fibers**. **Leigh syndrome**: subacute necrotizing encephalopathy in infancy.
cards.back_pt: **LHON** (neuropatia óptica hereditária de Leber): perda visual central indolor e subaguda nos dois olhos, sobretudo em homens jovens. **MELAS**: miopatia, encefalopatia, **acidose láctica**, episódios semelhantes a AVC. **MERRF**: epilepsia mioclônica, **fibras vermelhas rasgadas** (*ragged red fibers*). **Síndrome de Leigh**: encefalopatia necrosante subaguda na infância.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man is brought to the emergency department with confusion and heavy sweating. He has been taking a "fat-burning" powder bought online to lose weight before a bodybuilding contest. Temperature is 41.2°C (106.2°F), pulse is 134/min, respirations are 30/min, and blood pressure is 106/64 mm Hg. His pupils are normal in size and reactive. His skin has a yellow tint, but serum bilirubin is normal. Serum lactate is high, and there is an anion gap metabolic acidosis. His measured oxygen consumption is markedly increased. Which mechanism best explains his condition?
choices: Inhibition of cytochrome c oxidase (complex IV)
Blockade of the proton channel of ATP synthase
Return of protons into the mitochondrial matrix without passing ATP synthase
Release of norepinephrine from sympathetic nerve endings
questions.explanation: This is **2,4-dinitrophenol** poisoning, a banned weight-loss drug that also stains the skin yellow. It is an **uncoupler**: it carries protons back into the matrix, so the electron transport chain runs faster (**high O2 consumption**) while **ATP synthesis falls** and the energy becomes **heat**. A sympathomimetic also raises temperature and O2 use, but it usually causes **dilated pupils** and **hypertension**; here the pupils and blood pressure are normal, and the **yellow skin** points to DNP. Complex IV, complex I and ATP synthase inhibitors all **lower** O2 consumption.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de intoxicação por **2,4-dinitrofenol**, um emagrecedor proibido que também deixa a pele amarelada. Ele é um **desacoplador**: leva prótons de volta à matriz, então a cadeia de transporte de elétrons funciona mais rápido (**consumo de O2 alto**) enquanto a **síntese de ATP cai** e a energia vira **calor**. Um simpatomimético também eleva a temperatura e o consumo de O2, mas costuma causar **midríase** e **hipertensão**; aqui as pupilas e a pressão arterial estão normais, e a **pele amarelada** aponta para o DNP. Inibidores do complexo IV, do complexo I e da ATP sintase **reduzem** o consumo de O2.

questions.stem: A researcher studies isolated mitochondria in a buffer with succinate, ADP and inorganic phosphate. Oxygen consumption and ATP synthesis are both active. She adds compound X: oxygen consumption falls to a very low level and ATP synthesis stops. She then adds 2,4-dinitrophenol: oxygen consumption rises to above the starting level, but ATP synthesis does not return. Which compound is X most likely to be?
questions.explanation: **Oligomycin** blocks the proton channel of **ATP synthase**. Protons cannot flow back, the gradient becomes too steep, and electron transport slows. An **uncoupler** gives protons another way back, so O2 consumption returns, but ATP synthase stays blocked. Antimycin A, cyanide and malonate block the electron chain itself, so an uncoupler cannot restore O2 consumption. Rotenone blocks complex I, but succinate gives its electrons to **complex II**, so rotenone would have little effect here.
questions.explanation_pt: A **oligomicina** bloqueia o canal de prótons da **ATP sintase**. Os prótons não conseguem voltar, o gradiente fica muito alto e o transporte de elétrons diminui. Um **desacoplador** abre outro caminho para os prótons, então o consumo de O2 volta, mas a ATP sintase continua bloqueada. Antimicina A, cianeto e malonato bloqueiam a própria cadeia de elétrons, então um desacoplador não restaura o consumo de O2. A rotenona bloqueia o complexo I, mas o succinato entrega seus elétrons ao **complexo II**, então a rotenona teria pouco efeito aqui.

questions.stem: A 15-year-old boy has sudden jerks of his arms for 1 year and, recently, generalized seizures. He also has an unsteady gait and gets tired quickly when he exercises. Serum lactate is high at rest. His mother has mild muscle weakness. A muscle biopsy stained with Gomori trichrome shows many fibers with irregular red deposits under the cell membrane. These deposits are most likely made of which structure?
questions.explanation: Myoclonus, seizures, ataxia and **lactic acidosis** with a mildly affected mother suggest **MERRF**, a mitochondrial DNA disease. The red deposits are **ragged red fibers**: masses of abnormal **mitochondria** that collect under the sarcolemma as the cell tries to make up for poor oxidative phosphorylation. Glycogen builds up in glycogen storage myopathies such as McArdle disease, which cause cramps and no rise in lactate. Lipid droplets build up in fatty-acid oxidation defects.
questions.explanation_pt: Mioclonias, crises convulsivas, ataxia e **acidose láctica** com mãe levemente afetada sugerem **MERRF**, uma doença do DNA mitocondrial. Os depósitos vermelhos são **fibras vermelhas rasgadas** (*ragged red fibers*): acúmulos de **mitocôndrias** anormais sob o sarcolema, na tentativa da célula de compensar a fosforilação oxidativa deficiente. O glicogênio se acumula nas miopatias por depósito de glicogênio, como a doença de McArdle, que causam cãibras e não elevam o lactato. As gotículas de lipídio se acumulam nos defeitos de oxidação de ácidos graxos.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old man has painless loss of central vision in his right eye over 2 weeks. Six weeks later, the same happens in his left eye. Moving his eyes does not hurt. Visual fields show central scotomas in both eyes. Fundoscopy shows hyperemic, swollen-looking optic discs with small twisted vessels around them. MRI of the brain is normal. His maternal uncle and a cousin on his mother's side became blind in their twenties. A mutation in mitochondrial DNA is found. Which part of the respiratory chain is most likely affected?
questions.explanation: Sequential, painless central vision loss in a young man with affected maternal relatives suggests **Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON)**. The common LHON mutations are in mtDNA genes for subunits of **complex I** (NADH dehydrogenase). Complex II is wrong because all its subunits are encoded by **nuclear DNA**, so it cannot carry an mtDNA mutation. Complex V (ATP synthase) mtDNA mutations cause NARP and some cases of Leigh syndrome, not LHON.
questions.explanation_pt: Perda visual central indolor e sequencial em um homem jovem com parentes maternos afetados sugere **neuropatia óptica hereditária de Leber (LHON)**. As mutações comuns da LHON estão em genes do mtDNA para subunidades do **complexo I** (NADH desidrogenase). O complexo II está errado porque todas as suas subunidades são codificadas pelo **DNA nuclear**, então não pode ter uma mutação do mtDNA. Mutações do mtDNA no complexo V (ATP sintase) causam NARP e alguns casos de síndrome de Leigh, e não LHON.

notes.title: Mitochondrial energetics: TCA cycle, oxidative phosphorylation and mitochondrial disease
notes.body_md:
## TCA cycle

- Runs in the **mitochondrial matrix**. Per acetyl-CoA: **3 NADH, 1 FADH2, 1 GTP, 2 CO2**.
- Rate-limiting enzyme: **isocitrate dehydrogenase**. ADP and Ca2+ activate it; ATP and NADH inhibit it.
- **Alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase** uses the same cofactors as pyruvate dehydrogenase (B1, B2, B3, B5, lipoic acid).

## Electron transport and ATP synthase

- NADH gives electrons to **complex I**; FADH2 (from succinate) enters at **complex II**. Both pass through **CoQ**, complex III, cytochrome c and **complex IV**, which reduces O2 to water.
- Complexes I, III and IV pump protons. The **proton gradient** drives **ATP synthase**.
- About **2.5 ATP per NADH** and **1.5 ATP per FADH2**.

## Inhibitors vs uncouplers

- Chain inhibitors (rotenone, antimycin A, **cyanide**, **CO**) and **oligomycin**: O2 use and ATP both fall.
- **Uncouplers** (2,4-dinitrophenol, aspirin overdose, **thermogenin** in brown fat): O2 use rises, ATP falls, heat rises.

## Yield and quick energy

- About **32 ATP** per glucose (malate-aspartate shuttle) or **30** (glycerol-3-phosphate shuttle); anaerobic glycolysis gives **2**.
- **Creatine phosphate** in muscle quickly regenerates ATP in the first seconds of effort.

## Reactive oxygen species

- The chain leaks some **superoxide**. Defenses: **superoxide dismutase**, **catalase**, **glutathione peroxidase** (selenium) and NADPH-dependent glutathione reductase.
- Phagocytes make superoxide on purpose with **NADPH oxidase**; its loss causes chronic granulomatous disease (see immunology).

## Lactic acidosis

- When oxidative phosphorylation fails, pyruvate becomes **lactate**.
- Causes: shock and hypoxia, **cyanide**, **metformin**, thiamine deficiency, mitochondrial disease.

## Mitochondrial disease

- **Maternal inheritance** with **heteroplasmy** (patterns in medical genetics).
- Tissues with high energy needs suffer most: brain, muscle, retina and optic nerve.
- Examples: **LHON**, **MELAS**, **MERRF** (ragged red fibers), **Leigh syndrome**.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Ciclo de Krebs

- Ocorre na **matriz mitocondrial**. Por acetil-CoA: **3 NADH, 1 FADH2, 1 GTP, 2 CO2**.
- Enzima limitante: **isocitrato desidrogenase**. ADP e Ca2+ a ativam; ATP e NADH a inibem.
- A **alfa-cetoglutarato desidrogenase** usa os mesmos cofatores da piruvato desidrogenase (B1, B2, B3, B5, ácido lipoico).

## Transporte de elétrons e ATP sintase

- O NADH entrega elétrons ao **complexo I**; o FADH2 (do succinato) entra no **complexo II**. Ambos passam pela **CoQ**, complexo III, citocromo c e **complexo IV**, que reduz O2 a água.
- Os complexos I, III e IV bombeiam prótons. O **gradiente de prótons** move a **ATP sintase**.
- Cerca de **2,5 ATP por NADH** e **1,5 ATP por FADH2**.

## Inibidores vs desacopladores

- Inibidores da cadeia (rotenona, antimicina A, **cianeto**, **CO**) e **oligomicina**: consumo de O2 e ATP caem.
- **Desacopladores** (2,4-dinitrofenol, intoxicação por ácido acetilsalicílico, **termogenina** no tecido adiposo marrom): consumo de O2 sobe, ATP cai, calor aumenta.

## Rendimento e energia rápida

- Cerca de **32 ATP** por glicose (lançadeira malato-aspartato) ou **30** (lançadeira do glicerol-3-fosfato); a glicólise anaeróbia rende **2**.
- A **fosfocreatina** do músculo regenera ATP rapidamente nos primeiros segundos de esforço.

## Espécies reativas de oxigênio

- A cadeia libera um pouco de **superóxido**. Defesas: **superóxido dismutase**, **catalase**, **glutationa peroxidase** (selênio) e glutationa redutase dependente de NADPH.
- Os fagócitos produzem superóxido de propósito com a **NADPH oxidase**; sua perda causa a doença granulomatosa crônica (ver imunologia).

## Acidose láctica

- Quando a fosforilação oxidativa falha, o piruvato vira **lactato**.
- Causas: choque e hipóxia, **cianeto**, **metformina**, deficiência de tiamina, doença mitocondrial.

## Doença mitocondrial

- **Herança materna** com **heteroplasmia** (padrões em genética médica).
- Os tecidos com maior demanda de energia sofrem mais: cérebro, músculo, retina e nervo óptico.
- Exemplos: **LHON**, **MELAS**, **MERRF** (fibras vermelhas rasgadas), **síndrome de Leigh**.
